note: What the Software Factory pages can't measure from in-the-loop's published files yet, and what would let them. Shown on the methodology page; docs/software-factory-upstream.md has each request in full. Not part of a snapshot's identity.

requests.title: Loops while they run
requests.today: Only finished, published runs. Nothing says whether a loop is running now.
requests.ask: A reporter on the factory machine that publishes each active loop's cycle, last commit, last output and spend, with an expiry, as the runtime contract describes.

requests.title: Who sent each prompt
requests.today: Read from the start of each prompt's text against the loop's known templates, so a new template counts as a person until it is listed.
requests.ask: An origin field on each prompt in a session's metrics: person, loop harness, another agent, or interruption.

requests.title: Run records as data
requests.today: The source's loops index now gives every run's start, end and cycles, and the clock is drawn from it. A run's own record, opened on the clock, is still parsed from the markdown: its header, its cycle lines and its Ended line. Runs before 2026-11-06 and verification sessions have none, and open with what the index has: a run's cycles, and for a verification session only what it took, since the index ties no proof job to one.
requests.ask: A JSON record beside each markdown one: start, end, stop reason, cycle limit, and each cycle's change, time and decision.

requests.title: Code lines without a checkout
requests.today: Counted from git, so only a snapshot made from a checkout has them.
requests.ask: A published table of each change's lines added and removed per file class, written when the traces are.

requests.title: Rework by line age
requests.today: How much of each day's code still stands, from git blame at the published revision. Not when a line was replaced, or by which change.
requests.ask: For each change, how many earlier lines it replaced and how old they were, so rework within a day can be told from cleanup weeks later.

requests.title: What happened after a failed call
requests.today: Whether the next tool call in the session succeeded. The trace doesn't say whether that call was a retry.
requests.ask: For each failed call, the call that retried it, if any, and whether the retry succeeded.

requests.title: What review changed
requests.today: Nothing: the traces don't record review.
requests.ask: For each change, the review findings raised against it and the changes that answered them.
